newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA HIT BACK TO FORCE DRAW WITH LATVIA.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA HIT BACK TO FORCE DRAW WITH LATVIA.

text.p: Canada hit back with a pair of third-period goals to earn a 3-3 draw against Latvia at the world ice hockey championship on Wednesday.
Jarome Iginla's goal with less than five minutes remaining allowed Canada to escape with the draw and prevented Latvia from claiming their first world championship win in 58 years.
The result leaves Canada in third place in pool B on three points, three behind Sweden and the United States, who lead the standings with six.
It was the first point after two consecutive one-goal defeats for the Latvians, who are making their first appearance at the world championship as an independent nation since 1939.
Canada had trailed 3-1 going into the final period.

Mark Recchi, who joined the team on Monday after the Montreal Canadiens were eliminated from the Stanley Cup playoffs, pulled Canada to within one before Ignila batted a slapshot past Latvian netminder Juris Klodans to get the draw.
For the second straight game Canada proved to be their own worst enemy, both Latvia's second-period goals coming while they enjoyed a two-man advantage.
After Aleksandrs Kercs had scored the only goal of the first period to put Latvia 1-0 ahead, Los Angeles Kings defenceman Rob Blake quickly levelled the score just 33 seconds into the second period.
Kercs restored Latvia's lead midway through the middle period when he converted a two-man advantage, snapping a wrist shot through a crowd in front of the Canadian net.
Sergei Cudinovs sent Latvia into the second interval two in front when his long slap shot beat Sean Burke low to the stick side with just 57 seconds remaining in the period.
